name: Parity & Things That Stay Fixed
lesson: Parity means whether a whole number is even or odd. Adding an even number preserves parity; adding an odd number switches it.
An invariant is something that stays unchanged during a process. It might be a total, a remainder, a colour balance or whether a number is even.
To show that a task is impossible, find a property that every permitted move preserves, then check whether the target has that property.

problems.q: Is the sum of three odd whole numbers even or odd?
problems.solution: Two odd numbers add to an even number. Adding the third odd number makes the total odd.

problems.q: Is the product of an odd whole number and an even whole number even or odd?
problems.hint: An even factor contains a factor of 2.
problems.solution: The product still has a factor of 2, so it is even.

problems.q: Eight coins start heads up. Each move flips exactly two different coins. Can you finish with exactly one tail?
problems.hint: Track the parity of the number of tails.
problems.solution: Flipping two coins changes the number of tails by 2, 0 or -2. It stays even, so it cannot become 1.

problems.q: A 4 by 4 checkerboard has its top-left and bottom-right squares removed. Can the remaining board be covered by 1 by 2 dominoes with no overlap?
problems.hint: Each domino covers one light square and one dark square.
problems.solution: The removed corners have the same colour. There are now 6 squares of that colour and 8 of the other, so equal-colour pairs cannot cover the board.
problems.imageAlt: A four-by-four checkerboard with the top-left and bottom-right squares crossed out.

problems.q: A grasshopper starts at 0 on a number line. Each jump is either 4 units right or 6 units left. Can it land on 7?
problems.hint: Both permitted moves change the position by an even number.
problems.solution: The position remains even after every jump. Since 7 is odd, it cannot be reached.

problems.q: The numbers 1 through 10 are on a board. Repeatedly erase two numbers and replace them by their sum until one number remains. What is it?
problems.hint: The sum of all numbers on the board never changes.
problems.solution: The final number is the original total, $1+2+\cdots+10=55$.

problems.q: A jar starts with 17 counters. Each move either removes 2 counters or adds 4. Can the jar ever become empty?
problems.hint: Both moves preserve the parity of the counter total.
problems.solution: The total stays odd, while 0 is even. The jar cannot become empty.

problems.q: A 3 by 3 checkerboard has five dark squares and four light squares. One square is removed, then four dominoes cover the rest. What colour must the removed square have been?
problems.hint: Four dominoes need four squares of each colour.
problems.solution: Removing a dark square leaves four dark and four light squares. Removing a light square would leave unequal colour totals.

problems.q: The numbers 3, 7 and 10 are on a board. A move replaces two numbers with their positive difference or zero if equal. Can the final number be 0? Give a sequence.
problems.answer: Yes: replace 10 and 7 by 3, then 3 and 3 by 0.
problems.hint: Try making the two remaining numbers equal.
problems.solution: First $10-7=3$ leaves 3 and 3. Their difference is 0.

problems.q: Twenty lamps start off. Each move toggles exactly three different lamps. After exactly 11 moves, could all 20 lamps be on?
problems.hint: Each move changes the parity of the number of lamps that are on.
problems.solution: Toggling three lamps changes the on-count by an odd number. After 11 moves that count is odd, whereas 20 is even.

problems.q: A chess knight moves 2 squares in one direction and 1 at right angles. On a checkerboard it changes colour on every move. Can it return to its starting square after exactly 15 moves?
problems.hint: Compare the starting and ending colours.
problems.solution: After an odd number of colour changes, the knight is on the opposite colour. Its starting square has the original colour, so a 15-move return is impossible.

problems.q: The numbers 1 through 9 are on a board. Each move erases two numbers $a,b$ and writes $a+b-1$. After eight moves, what is the remaining number?
problems.hint: Track how much the total falls on each move.
problems.solution: The initial sum is 45. Each move decreases the total by 1. After eight moves, one number remains and equals $45-8=37$.
